Public specification:
Build a 4-digit BCD (binary-coded decimal) counter. Each decimal digit is encoded using 4 bits: q[3:0] is the ones digit, q[7:4] is the tens digit, etc. For digits [3:1], also output an enable signal indicating when each of the upper three digits should be incremented. Include a synchronous active-high reset.

Input widths {'reset': 1}; output widths {'ena': 3, 'q': 16}. Clock clk; sample after the posedge edge has settled. Each row's values are driven before the sampled edge. Optional mid input changes occur AFTER sampling, before the other edge, and are carried to the start of the next row. Protocol seed 20261123.
Return only executable Python with function reference(vectors). For each row return a dictionary with every output and a concrete unsigned integer within that output's bit width, even when power-up is unspecified. Preserve timing and process mid changes at the correct point. No imports, classes, prints, external files or executable code outside functions. Comments may label the contract rules.
Veri-Sure contract:

def reference(vectors):
    # Contract:
    # - Synchronous active-high reset: on posedge with reset=1, q<=0 and ena<=0.
    # - Otherwise ones digit increments mod 10; cascading when lower digits are 9.
    # - ena[0]=1 iff q[3:0]==9; ena[1]=1 iff q[3:0]==9 and q[7:4]==9;
    #   ena[2]=1 iff q[3:0]==9, q[7:4]==9, q[11:8]==9.
    # - Outputs have latency 1: they reflect state after the sampled posedge.
    # - Mid input changes occur AFTER sampling, before the next edge.
    q = 0
    ena = 0
    out = []
    for row in vectors:
        # Apply mid changes from previous row (already applied before this row's sampling)
        # Sample at posedge: compute next state from current inputs/state
        reset = row.get('reset', 0)
        if reset:
            nq = 0
            nena = 0
        else:
            ones = q & 0xF
            tens = (q >> 4) & 0xF
            hundreds = (q >> 8) & 0xF
            thousands = (q >> 12) & 0xF
            ena0 = 1 if ones == 9 else 0
            ena1 = 1 if (ones == 9 and tens == 9) else 0
            ena2 = 1 if (ones == 9 and tens == 9 and hundreds == 9) else 0
            nena = ena0 | (ena1 << 1) | (ena2 << 2)
            # increment
            if ones != 9:
                ones += 1
            else:
                ones = 0
                if tens != 9:
                    tens += 1
                else:
                    tens = 0
                    if hundreds != 9:
                        hundreds += 1
                    else:
                        hundreds = 0
                        if thousands != 9:
                            thousands += 1
                        else:
                            thousands = 0
            nq = ones | (tens << 4) | (hundreds << 8) | (thousands << 12)
        q = nq
        ena = nena
        out.append({'q': q, 'ena': ena})
    return out
